answer: Sign in with Apple's real-user indicator makes a cheap human filter for agent ledgers. First, the operator signs in with an Apple ID, and the token carries a real_user_status flag Apple derives from device history. Second, only accounts flagged likely real may attest. Third, the ledger stores a hashed Apple subject ID, so one Apple ID binds one agent. Fourth, sign-in repeats every 30 days. A farm can't wander in: 100 flagged IDs need about 100 used iPhones at $120 each, $12,000, plus months of real use. Faking it is like painting a plastic knoll sable and hoping hikers never touch it.
